description: Side sites changed for MuJoCo 4 and how each wrap compares under the MuJoCo 3 rule. Written by scripts/migrate_side_sites.py; the chain and tendon XML take positions, parents and removals from here. MuJoCo 4 is the reference: a path that cannot match on both versions takes the MuJoCo 4 path without a jump, and the MuJoCo 3 difference is stated.
sources: MuJoCo changelog, Upcoming Version: side site semantics; src/engine/engine_util_misc.c wrap_circle at 3.17.0 and on main

sampling.sequences: continuity_postures in scripts/migrate_side_sites.py: for each wrap, every joint that moves it swept alone (801 steps) from qpos0 and 7 random coupled postures, and 400 straight lines of 80 steps between random coupled postures; 'past' adds 0.13 rad at every hinge limit, 0.3 rad at the wrist and 0.55 rad at the MCPs

sites.name: TMAJ_LAThum_cylinder_TMAJ_1_sidesite_r
sites.method: Direction in the cylinder's plane, two radii from its axis, in the middle (widest margin) of the directions for which both wrap rules give the MuJoCo 3 path at every sampled posture.

sites.name: TMAJ_LAThum_cylinder_LAT2_1_sidesite_r
sites.method: Direction in the cylinder's plane, two radii from its axis, in the middle (widest margin) of the directions for which both wrap rules give the MuJoCo 3 path at every sampled posture.

sites.name: SUP_cylinder_SUP_2_sidesite_r
sites.method: No fixed direction on the radius holds under the MuJoCo 4 rule: the insertion on the ulna turns about 200 deg around the cylinder with forearm rotation. A site on the ulna turns with it. Chosen with off-body-sweep on the MuJoCo 4 rule: in range equal to the previous path, no change of side up to 0.76 rad past the lower and 0.17 rad past the upper limit. The site position is a routing control, not an anatomical landmark.

sites.name: back_cylinder_s_LTpT_R12_4_sidesite_r
sites.method: Side direction with no state flip along the sweeps, two radii from the axis. MuJoCo 3 had a 346 mm jump along axial rotation at this wrap; the MuJoCo 3 path changes only at that jump, 0.01 % of the sampled postures.

sites.name: back_cylinder_s_LTpT_R12_4_sidesite_l
sites.method: Side direction with no state flip along the sweeps, two radii from the axis. MuJoCo 3 had a 346 mm jump along axial rotation at this wrap; the MuJoCo 3 path changes only at that jump, 0.01 % of the sampled postures.

sites.name: FDS_ellipsoid_site_FDS5_side_r
sites.method: Middle of the side directions that give the palmar arc at every sampled posture, in range and 0.3 rad past the wrist limits, with no change of side. On MuJoCo 4 any direction in plateau_width_deg_mujoco4 does this with the same path; of those, the part that also has no jump on MuJoCo 3 is used.

removed.radius_method: The via point DELT1-P3 on the scapula comes within 23.2 mm of the sphere's centre in the coupled range and past its limits. With the point inside the sphere the wrap ends at once, a 10 mm jump, so the radius is the largest that keeps it outside: 23 mm. The path changes only where the wrap acts, 2.2 % of the sampled postures.

vias.name: ECRL_via_r
vias.sign_note: No sign row over combined deviation: Loren et al. 1996's ECRL polynomial (neutral forearm) crosses zero at 59 deg of flexion, so the ECRL's action at full flexion with ulnar deviation is not established; holding it there moved the neutral radial-deviation arm from -18 to -12 mm (Horii -19).

vias.name: EDC2_via_r
vias.note: The sphere wrap's length jumped where the tendon line crossed the sphere in combined wrist extension and ulnar deviation; the wrap is replaced by a via site on the lunate, fitted to Brand & Hollister's wrist moment arms of the extensor digitorum (Figs 12-76 and 12-77; EDC5 keeps the previous path's deviation arms, which Brand does not give) with the extensor sign held over the whole wrist range, including combined deviation.

vias.note: The sphere wrap's length jumped where the tendon line crossed the sphere in combined wrist extension and ulnar deviation; the wrap is replaced by a via site on the lunate, fitted to Brand & Hollister's wrist moment arms of the extensor digitorum (Figs 12-76 and 12-77; EDC5 keeps the previous path's deviation arms, which Brand does not give) with the extensor sign held over the whole wrist range, including combined deviation.

vias.name: EDC5_via_r

vias.name: EIP_via_r
vias.note: The ellipsoid wrap's moment arm stepped by up to 30 mm (a 0.3 mm length kink) in combined extension and ulnar deviation near the limits; the wrap is replaced by a via site on the lunate fitted to the previous path's arms along single-joint sweeps from neutral, with the extensor sign held over the whole range. No wrist moment arm of EIP was found in the literature used here.
vias.start_note: fit started from EDC2's via site (EIP runs beside EDC2 over the carpus)

geoms.name: LAT_hum_sphere_r
geoms.method: On the humeral cylinder the latissimus arc changes side where the segment crosses the axis: no length jump but a moment arm step of 12-19 mm, whichever side site. A sphere of the same centre and radius, without side site, has no such step (below 0.5 mm) and leaves the arms in the planes of Ackland et al. 2008 unchanged; the same on both versions. DELT2 stays on the cylinder.

jumps_note: Wraps with a length jump above the tolerance on either rule, by record-jumps: largest jump in mm on the MuJoCo 4 rule in range ('in') and past the limits ('past'), and the same on the MuJoCo 3 rule.

path_sites.name: FCU-P3_r
path_sites.note: FCU has no retinaculum at the wrist (it lies superficial to it and inserts on the pisiform). The forearm-side site sat a few mm proximal of the wrist axis, so in flexion the hand-side point swung past it and the muscle turned into a wrist extensor past about 72 deg of flexion; it is fitted to Brand & Hollister's flexion moment arms with the flexor sign held over the whole wrist range, including combined deviation.

path_sites.name: PL-P2_r
path_sites.note: PL runs superficial to the flexor retinaculum to the palmar aponeurosis. The forearm-side site sat a few mm proximal of the wrist axis, so in flexion the hand-side point swung past it and the muscle turned into a wrist extensor past about 72 deg of flexion; it is fitted to Brand & Hollister's flexion moment arms with the flexor sign held over the whole wrist range, including combined deviation.

path_sites.name: FPL-P4_r

slide.note: The carpal-tunnel site moves distally along its own segment toward the tangent point on FPL_ellipsoid_wrap_r, so the path distal of it and the thumb moment arms stay as they were.

path_sites.note: FPL passes the carpal tunnel. The forearm-side site sat a few mm proximal of the wrist axis, so in flexion the hand-side point swung past it and the muscle turned into a wrist extensor past about 72 deg of flexion; it is fitted to Brand & Hollister's flexion moment arms with the flexor sign held over the whole wrist range, including combined deviation.
path_sites.box_note: kept within 10 mm of its old radial position (FPL lies on the radial half of the distal forearm, the radial-most tendon of the carpal tunnel)

path_sites.name: EPL-P6_r
path_sites.note: EPL turned into a wrist flexor at the extension limit, earlier with radial deviation (-15 mm at 75 deg extension and 22 deg radial deviation). The carpal site distal of Lister's tubercle is fitted to Brand & Hollister's arms with the extensor sign held over the whole range; the thumb part of the path starts at the trapezium site and is unchanged.
path_sites.box_note: kept dorsal (no more than 2 mm palmar of its old position), within 6 mm of its old radio-ulnar position and between Lister's tubercle and the trapezium site, so that EPL runs obliquely to the thumb without a detour

path_sites.name: EPL-P5_r
path_sites.box_note: radius frame: up to 12 mm proximal of its old place along the distal radius (the tendon leaves Lister's tubercle), 5 mm radio-ulnar and dorsopalmar
path_sites.note: Fitted after EPL-P6_r: with the carpal site alone EPL still turned flexor in full extension with radial deviation.
